title: Showing off

segments.voice: Yesterday, hasad, envy, and your line: pray for them. Whose good news did you say a good word for? Day one thousand two hundred eighty-four.

Who was watching the last time you did something good? Not a trick question. A door held, a donation, a long prayer, a kind comment under someone's post. Sometimes nobody saw. Sometimes the whole room did. The deed looks the same either way. The Qur'an has a short surah, al-Ma'un, that turns on exactly this. It speaks of worshippers who pray, and still it says woe to them, because of why they pray. Today, the disease that can live inside a good deed: showing off, what Arabic calls riya'.

First, a callback to ikhlas, four days ago: actions are by intentions, the hadith that opens Sahih al-Bukhari. Riya' is the same good deed, aimed at the wrong eyes. Second, the surah. Pickthall's words: "Ah, woe unto worshippers Who are heedless of their prayer; Who would be seen (at worship)". Then comes the twist at the end: they would be seen, and yet they refuse small kindnesses. The prayer done for an audience sits right next to a hand that won't pass the salt. Showing off and stinginess, in that surah, keep company. Third, a picture from al-Baqarah. Charity given to be seen by people is like a smooth rock with a little soil on it. Heavy rain comes, and the rock is left bare. Nothing could take root. And fourth, the cure, which is not hiding everything. The Qur'an praises those who give by night and by day, in secret and openly. Public good can teach and invite. But one hadith, in Sahih al-Bukhari, describes a person Allah shades on a day with no other shade: someone who gives charity so quietly that the left hand doesn't know what the right hand gave. So the practice isn't never be seen. It's keep a few good deeds where only Allah sees them, so the heart remembers who they were for.
screen: `BY INTENTIONS.` · `WHO WOULD BE SEEN.` · `SOIL ON A SMOOTH ROCK.` · then, large: `THE LEFT HAND DOESN'T KNOW.`

segments.voice: The practice: keep one good private. Settle, and breathe. Choose one good thing you can do today that nobody will find out about. Pay for something anonymously. Fix something someone else broke and say nothing. Pray a little longer when no one is near. Pick it now, and see it done. Then notice the small itch to mention it later, and let the itch be. If you pray, you can ask that it be accepted. If you don't, let the deed be enough without a witness. The bell holds the time.
Showing off. Riya': doing good in order to be seen; in the Qur'an, soil on a smooth rock that the rain washes away. Today's word.

Your line: not for eyes. Do the hidden good you chose, and don't tell anyone, not even a hint. Tomorrow, a disease that burns hot and fast: the fire of anger. Day one thousand two hundred eighty-four.

howItsDone: Muslim teachers warn against riya', doing good to be seen, starting from the hadith that actions are by intentions; some keep part of their charity and extra prayer private, while public giving is also praised in the Qur'an.
